turns.assessment: The svc273 failure belongs to the broad event at t=665 s, not the unrelated och91 card failure at S14 at t=602.5 s. Every channel on OMS S10→S21 disappeared, with loss already present at the booster input and unchanged pump currents; this localizes the failure ahead of amp0 rather than to an amplifier or downstream span. A pulled/broken OMS input patch at S10 best explains the simultaneous all-channel hard loss and downstream AMP_INPUT_LOS/OCH_LOS cascade.

proposals.rationale: The input and output optical powers of amp0 and all downstream amplifiers were lost while pump currents did not change. E1 is the common point immediately before amp0, and a disconnected input patch produces exactly this all-channel hard loss.

A ROADM port failure at S10 could remove light before the booster, but a single WSS input-port failure would not normally block channels arriving through multiple degrees, making it less consistent with the broad channel set.
A cut in span0 would explain the amp1 input LOS and downstream losses, but amp0 input was also lost and the reverse-direction OMS remained normal, both arguing against this location.
A failed booster could remove all downstream channels, but it would not explain loss at its own input, and its pump-current telemetry showed no change.
